title: Premium Arrears, the Grace Period and Reinstatement on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan
content:
A drug plan premium still unpaid after its due day puts a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan enrollment into the premium grace period, and the member is sent a notice naming the amount owed and the last day of that grace period.

## Counting the grace period

The grace period runs for the number of calendar days the plan held fixes, counted from the day the plan posted the first unpaid drug plan premium charge. Coverage is ended for non-payment only where the plan has not received the full outstanding premium by the last day of that grace period, counted from that same day. Calendar days are counted from the day after that posting date, every day of the week counts including weekends and public holidays, the last day of the grace period is itself still inside the grace period, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days.

| The day the outstanding premium reaches the plan | Whether the grace period is still open |
| --- | --- |
| The day before the last day of the grace period | open |
| The last day of the grace period itself | open |
| The day after the last day of the grace period | closed |

## While the delinquency runs

- Where the full outstanding amount reaches the plan before the last day of the grace period ends, the enrollment returns to being in force with no break, and the member keeps their accumulated out-of-pocket total and their payment stage.
- A partial payment does not cure the delinquency and never restarts the clock, however small the remainder.
- While the enrollment is in the grace period the member's prescriptions are still covered and priced normally; the plan never turns a member away at the pharmacy for premium arrears.

## Termination and reinstatement

Termination for non-payment ends drug coverage on the last day of the month in which the grace period expired, and the member is told that a gap in drug coverage may add to a future late enrollment penalty.

A member terminated for non-payment may ask to be reinstated where the failure to pay was caused by circumstances beyond their control, and the request must reach the plan inside the reinstatement window of the plan held, counted from the coverage end date. Reinstatement is granted only on a good-cause determination recorded by the plan's reviewer, and restores the original coverage effective date with no gap, so the member keeps the out-of-pocket total and payment stage they had reached; the member's own account of why they could not pay opens the review but never decides it. Money arriving from a terminated member is held rather than posted while that review runs, and is returned in full where reinstatement is refused.
